items.title: 68251_Teddy McRae oral history interview
items.q: Now the same time we worked the Savoy with Coleman Hawkins -- Erskine Hawkins Band

ctx.x: S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943

Very clean gentleman. Most of the musicians that you are reading about or talking about, these fellows were just like -- (inaudible) just like doctors. They carried theirself as gentleman -- you know, musicians back there. Thought very highly of themselves. If we went out in the afternoons Hampton, they would dress, like, you know.

First time I saw Coleman Hawkins walking down 7th Avenue, he had on this black coat -- dark gray coat with striped pants and his walking cane. Guy say (inaudible), "That's Coleman Hawkins." I say (inaudible), "No." (Inaudible), "Coleman, hi." He'd say, "Hi," you know. Very classy (inaudible). You know, (inaudible). And those are the days that musicians thought of -- everybody respect them, you know. and (inaudible) everybody looked up to the musicians in that (inaudible) day, you know -- you know, back in those…

items.title: 68251_Teddy McRae oral history interview
items.q: Willie (Inaudible) Smith -- all the top men in there, you know.

ctx.x: That happened one night back in the Charlie Johnson days (inaudible). That's when Fletcher had that tremendous band at the Roseland.
Willie (Inaudible) Smith -- all the top men in there, you know. His wife called me to come down. Coleman didn't show up that night.
